newsitem.title: USA: Pennzoil CEO sees energy prices up -report.
newsitem.headline: Pennzoil CEO sees energy prices up -report.

text.p: Pennzoil Chief Executive Officer James Pate expects higher average energy prices next year and higher output, Barron's reported.
The financial weekly said the higher energy prices should translate into higher profits for Pennzoil, which produces oil and natural gas, makes motor oil and operates the Jiffy Lube franchise.
Every increase of $0.10 per thousand cubic feet of natural gas translates into $0.38 a share in earnings for Pennzoil, Barron's said.

Higher natural gas prices have helped the company in the near-term, but early this year it had hedged its production through futures contracts, Barron's said. Despite missing the benefits of higher gas and oil prices this year, the company repaid $300 million in debt, Barron's said.

Pate told Barron's that a big contributor the Pennzoil's output should be from its 75 percent-owned West Cameron 580 block in the Gulf of Mexico, which is expected to yield 80 million cubic feet of gas per day.

In the long-term, Pennzoil's stakes in exploration and development of two sites offshore Azerbaijan could be a huge boom for the company, since oil reserves are estimated to be several billion barrels, Barron's said.
